messages:
maria-cust: we're seeing intermittent 502/connection timeouts to our internal endpoint api.prod.internal.redwood from services in the customer's VPC. started around 2026-03-11T14:02Z, affects ~30% of hosts in us-west-2

sam-support: can you paste the curl/dig outputs and the VPC id? any recent infra changes or cross-account ops? :eyes:

maria-cust: from a customer EC2: 
```
$ curl -v https://api.prod.internal.redwood/health
*   Trying 10.0.5.22:443...
* connect to 10.0.5.22 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to api.prod.internal.redwood port 443: Connection timed out
```
and dig: 
```
$ dig +short api.prod.internal.redwood

;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 23456
```
VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d (acct 123456789012)

jamie-sre: NXDOMAIN from Route53 usually means the private hosted zone resolved to a different zone or there are no records. any chance someone associated a different private zone with the same name to that VPC?

maria-cust: customer notes a cross-account assoc last night at 2026-03-11T13:55Z but they thought it was for a different internal name. i'll pull route53 hosted zones now.

alice-engineering: note: Route53 private hosted zones are VPC-scoped. If two zones share the same name and both are associated to the VPC, the resolver picks one (last assoc wins) which can shadow the authoritative records. Common pitfall with cross-account sharing.

jamie-sre: run these (control account with creds) and paste output: 
```
aws route53 list-hosted-zones | jq -r '.HostedZones[] | "\(.Name) \(.Id)"'
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id /hostedzone/ZABC... --query 'VPCs'
# and on partner account for their zone id
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id /hostedzone/ZDEF... --query 'VPCs'
```
Also check resolver rules: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules` and endpoints.

sam-support: also `aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections` in case there is peering + overlapping private zones.

maria-cust: quick audit found two private hosted zones named "api.prod.internal.redwood." ours contains the A records; partner acct 987654321098 has a zone with same name but empty (no A/alias records). partner associated their zone to vpc-0a1b2c3d yesterday.

devops-bot: automated event: hosted zone ZZZZZ associated with vpc-0a1b2c3d in acct 987654321098 at 2026-03-11T13:54:59Z

jamie-sre: confirmed root cause: cross-account private hosted zone shadowing. When resolver hits the partner zone (which has no records for api.prod.internal.redwood) it answers NXDOMAIN. Two remediation options: (1) disassociate partner zone from the VPC (fast rollback) or (2) add the missing records to partner zone or create a resolver rule forwarding that name to the authoritative account.

sam-support: what's faster for the customer? they want immediate recovery.

maria-cust: they can't edit partner account. they asked us to request partner infra to remove the assoc. i don't have partner perms.

jamie-sre: i'll open a cross-account ops request. in parallel we can ask partner to add a temporary A record pointing to our LB so queries resolve while they remove the assoc. which is quicker for them?

sam-support: filing P1 with partner infra, including required ARNs and repro steps. also adding a short-term alert: increase in NXDOMAIN ratio for api.prod.internal.redwood > 0.5% triggers SMS.

maria-cust: partner removed association at 2026-03-11T14:10Z (confirmed). after removal dig returns our A records and curl /health succeeds from their EC2. customer verified app traffic restored.

alice-engineering: follow-ups: 1) add an infra guardrail to block duplicate private zone names across accounts / VPCs or require explicit approval, 2) document resolver-rule based forwarding runbook for cross-account ownership, 3) add a pre-assoc check in our internal request workflow to detect name collisions.

jamie-sre: creating GH issue INFRA-872 to track guardrail and runbook. saving timeline and attach logs to incident doc.

sam-support: closing P1 with RCA: cause = cross-account private hosted zone shadowing -> NXDOMAIN for internal service name; remediation = partner zone disassociated; recommend governance + resolver-forwarding for long-term. I'll send the RCA to customer.

maria-cust: thanks all, customer happy. will share short RCA and ask partner for a post-change review. :tada:
